title: Astro Portal API v1 observation-session event ingestion
description: The wire shape of POST /v1/sessions/{id}/events and of the event page a reader syncs back. This file owns the API-level ENVELOPE only — identity, type, clocks, origin. The body of each event is owned by the event-type registry under schemas/session-events/, referenced from $defs.eventPayloadByType, which is the single place a reader or a merge has to look at. `originDeviceId` is never accepted from a client: it is derived from the authenticated credential, exactly as tenant identity is.

eventId.description: A 26-character Crockford base32 ULID, the same rule as the registry's event envelope. Client events carry a client-generated ULID. An event generated by a debriefing or by an accepted supplement carries a ULID that is a pure function of STORED values only — the observation session's id, the frozen payload, its revision and the derived night start — and of nothing in the request: its 48-bit time part is the night anchor plus the event's own emission ordinal, and its 80-bit tail is the hash of the session id and a stable mapping key. It deliberately does NOT encode `recordedAt`, which may legitimately differ between two surfaces answering the same night; encoding it would let a race write the same event twice. Identity only: order events by recordedAt, then receivedAt, then eventId. See api/v1.md, "Deterministic event identifiers".

eventType.description: A key of the event-type registry (schemas/session-events/). The list is closed for a submission: an unrecognized type is rejected per event, never per batch. A READER of stored events, on the other hand, MUST tolerate a type it does not know (a newer service may store one): it shows an ordinary report, never an error.

eventPayloadByType.description: The registry dispatch, and the only cross-file coupling of this contract. Each branch delegates the payload OBJECT of one event type to that type's schema. A validator that cannot resolve a branch's target treats it as unconstrained, so this file is testable before the registry branch is merged.

submittedEnvelope.description: The registry's own event envelope (session-events/event-envelope.schema.json), restated here as this contract's wire shape. The two MUST agree; `submittedEvent` pins both at once so any drift between them fails loudly instead of silently, and so this file stays checkable on its own.

batchRequest.description: POST /v1/sessions/{id}/events. At most 500 events per batch; a larger batch is refused whole, with nothing written, because the size is a transport fault and not a fact about the night.

rejectionCode.description: Why one event of the batch was not stored. The batch itself still succeeds.

batchResponse.description: Every submitted event is accounted for in exactly one of `accepted`, `duplicate` and `rejected`; their sizes sum to the submitted count. `duplicate` means the (sessionId, eventId) pair already existed and the stored event was left untouched, whatever the resubmitted payload said. `clockSkewMs` is receivedAt minus the newest submitted recordedAt, offered so a device can correct its own clock display.

timing.description: What kind of claim this event's `recordedAt` makes. ADDITIVE and SERVER-SET: it is never accepted from a client, so the registry's submitted envelope is untouched and a device keeps sending exactly what it sent before. `observed` — the instant was measured: a device's own clock for an event the person recorded in the field, or the server clock for a note actually written at debriefing time. `planned` — the instant was READ OFF THE PLAN'S TIME SLOT (`nightStartAt` plus the item's `startMinute`/`endMinute`) and nobody measured it. `reconstructed` — the instant is a session-level fallback applied to an act that has no time of its own: the window the person declared at debriefing, the derived night boundaries, the night-of anchor, or an accepted supplement's `createdAt`. An interface MUST NOT present a `planned` or `reconstructed` instant as a measured time. A portal predating this field omits it; a reader that finds it absent learns nothing new and falls back to the only signal it already had, `originDeviceId === null` for a server-generated event.

source.description: Additive, SERVER-SET: where the event comes from. `astro-sync` — it was sent by a device of the application Astro Sync (a detection); `declared` — anything else (a person's gesture on the phone or the web, a debriefing, a rework). Derived from the authenticated credential, never accepted from a client, like `originDeviceId`; a service predating this field omits it, and a reader that finds it absent says nothing about the origin (never « Détecté par Astro Sync »).

reworkMark.description: Additive: present on a stored event only when the correction layer of a rework (`session-rework.schema.json`) touched it. `added` is true for an event a rework added (the only events a rework may remove); `targetId` is the target the event is posed on after the rework (a target of the session, `null` = the whole night). Additive: `replaces` is on an event that replaces another (a signal the person modified: the original stays in the log and is hidden from the effective events); `replacedBy` is on an event a later revision replaced, read only when a request asks for the replaced events and in the data export. A signal posed on a target a rework took out reads `targetId: null` (the whole night) unless a move places it elsewhere. An event no rework touched has no `rework`, and its target is the one its payload says, if any. The stored events a session page reads are the **effective** events: the append-only journal read through the correction layer.

replaces.description: The id of the event this one replaces (a signal the person modified).

removed.description: True on a logged event of a kind Astro Sync detects that a rework removed; read only when a request asks for the replaced events (`?includeReplaced=true`) and in the data export. Such an event is left out of the effective events.

replacedBy.description: The id of the event that replaces this one; read only when a request asks for the replaced events (`?includeReplaced=true`) and in the data export.

eventPage.description: GET /v1/sessions/{id}/events (additive). Ordered by receivedAt then eventId — the server clock, so the page is stable whatever a device's own clock claimed. `since` compares against receivedAt and is inclusive. "Session" is always the observation session here.
